title: Internal conjugation of resolving constraint edges and units
statement: Let Λ be a commutative condensed ring and assume the unbounded derived section-module categories exist for every scheme. For a scheme morphism f:X→Y use the fixed section cochain tensor, transported derived tensor, localization Q, exact section pullback F, derived pullback L and its natural isomorphism ε: Q⋙L ≅ F⋙Q, binary maps s=modelTensor over Y and t=modelTensor over X, ordinary oplax tensor arrow β and scalar unit u, and localized regular-unit isomorphisms eY,eX of [def-pd-section-resolving-oplax-constraint-data]. Let μ be a natural tensor arrow L(M⊗N)→LM⊗LN and let v:LQ(1)→Q(1). Assume SectionHypotheses, namely for every flat-term K-flat pair A,B the equation μ(QA,QB)≫(εA⊗εB)≫t(FA,FB) = L(s(A,B))≫ε(A⊗B)≫Q(β(A,B)), and v=ε(1)≫Q(u). Composition here is in Lean order. Let δ be an internal derived tensor arrow and w an internal regular-unit arrow. Assume Conjugation Λ f μ v δ w: its pair equation is precisely RepresentativeEquations for the fixed internal-to-section derived equivalences G,K, inverse γ, inverse θ, and δ; its unit equation uses L(regularY).hom≫v≫regularX.inv. Then for all internal derived objects M,N,H the six InternalEdges Λ f μ δ M N H squares hold, and for all internal derived objects M the full InternalUnits Λ f μ v δ w M proposition holds. The fixed internal and section vertices are those prescribed by nested inverse θ and inverse γ, with identity transported unit comparisons, and retain their resolving normalization.

proof.text: Use the ConstraintCondition of lem-pd-section-kflat-tensor-comparison. The fixed transported monoidal structure equals the canonical equivalence transport. Inverting its prescribed oplax tensor maps gives monoidal structures on G and K with identity unit maps and lax tensor maps exactly internalModelTensor, i.e. inverse theta. Expand Conjugation to obtain the binary representative equation at every pair of internal derived objects and its regular-unit equation. No resolution compatibility theorem for gamma is needed: gamma is the fixed natural isomorphism already appearing in the definitions.

proof.text: Prove the six edge squares generically for lax monoidal q,r and a natural tensor arrow mu. For the source associator use lax associativity for q and naturality of epsilon. For each outer splitting edge use naturality of mu along the source tensor comparison, then its binary representative equation. For each inner edge combine tensor compositions, substitute the binary equation, and use lax tensor naturality for r. For the target associator use associator naturality in epsilon and lax associativity for r. Specialize to G,K and inverse gamma with the normalized inverse theta maps; these are exactly InternalEdges.

proof.text: Compose the three left and three right SectionUnitEdges supplied by lem-pd-section-resolving-oplax-unit-models. The ordinary cochain unit identities from lem-pd-section-oplax-total-comparison identify those composites with the opposite branches; cancel the final epsilon component. Normalize the regular unit by naturality of mu along regular.hom, obtaining the ordinary unit axioms with eta = L(regularY.hom) followed by v and regularX.inv. Every section derived object is isomorphic to Q(P) for a flat-term K-flat P, by lem-pc-kflat-resolution and essential surjectivity of Q. Convert categorical tensor flatness into the site-flat predicate using siteSheafTensorRightIso from lem-weil-pbc-independent-sheaf-tensor-colimits. Transport both unit axioms along this isomorphism using the proved oplax unit invariance lemmas in WeilConjectures.CategoryTheory.Monoidal.OplaxOfLaxSquare.

proof.text: Prove the internal unit edge squares generically. The binary Conjugation equation gives the first edges, its unit equation and lax tensor naturality give the second, and normalized lax unitors with epsilon naturality give the third and opposite branches. All vertex maps are isomorphisms because G,K are monoidal and inverse gamma is an isomorphism. The unit comparisons here are identities, so the section unit laws already proved are exactly the whole-path unit equalities at G(M). Compose the three edges on each side to obtain the remaining whole-path formulas. Assemble all twenty clauses of InternalUnits and pair them with the six InternalEdges clauses.
